meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ыграть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to play along', paired with 'подыгрывать'.

examples.text: Бывший мой попросил, чтобы я подыграла ему.
examples.trans: My ex asked me to play along for him.

examples.text: Просто бывший мой попросил, чтобы я подыграла ему.
examples.trans: My ex simply asked me to play along for him.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of; from behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to threaten', paired with 'пригрозить'.

examples.trans: They threaten to leave without paying.

examples.text: Она из-за вас грозилась из дома уйти.
examples.trans: Because of you, she was threatening to move out of the apartment.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from, out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'house; building; home' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There's a new building on Simashko Street.

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, go away', paired with 'уходить'.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'have'.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

examples.text: Моя мама имела право на квартиру. Она пенсионерка.
examples.trans: My mother had a right to the flat. She is a pensioner.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'offer, proposal; sentence' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It's a good offer, of course.

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

поесть.gloss: to eat, to have a meal

meanings.en: to eat, to have a meal
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat, to have a meal', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Ну ладно, брось! Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: Oh come on, stop it! We'll only eat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'metro' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The metro station is located nearby.
You had better put a sign near the metro!

examples.text: Тогда встречаемся в семь часов около метро.
examples.trans: Then we meet at seven o'clock near the metro.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stand', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish drinking', paired with 'допивать'.

examples.trans: You didn't even finish your tea.
He finished his coffee and stood up.

examples.text: Но вы даже не допили чай.
examples.trans: But you did not even finish your tea.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for nothing, in vain', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'offense, resentment, hurt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will not forget this insult.
She was left with bitter resentment.

examples.text: Я всё равно не забуду эту обиду.
examples.trans: I will not forget this insult anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'face; person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He has a very kind face.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.
